prerequisites: LANGL1272 or a course of a similar level with a scientific orientation, equivalent to level B2- in speaking, B1 in writing, B2+ in listening comprehension and C1 in reading comprehension.

learning_outcomes.text: Communicate in English in speaking and writing with a good level of ease and precision in general, academic and professional contexts.
Master the necessary skills to pursue their studies in English at the master’s level.
Acquire speaking skills aligning with level B2+ (advanced) of the Common European Framework of Reference.
Acquire writing skills aligning with level B2- of the Common European Framework of Reference.
Contribute to the development, acquisition and evaluation of learning outcomes AA 4.3, 4.4, 4.5.
Contribute to the development, acquisition and evaluation of learning outcomes AA 5.1.

syllabus_topics: Language skills: general and specific vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation

Language functions for oral communication: introducing, structuring, explaining, going into details, opposing, negotiating, concluding, agreeing or disagreeing, interrupting, managing an informal discussion or a formal meeting, expressing an opinion, quoting sources, citing numbers, describing graphs, etc.
Interaction in general, academic and professional situations
Oral presentations linked to the UN's sustainable development goals
teaching_methods: Informal speaking practice through discussions on general or scientific topics chosen by students
Listening comprehension practice with videos shared by students in preparation of discussions
Formal speaking practice through debates on topics relating to engineering
Reading comprehension practice through the preparation work for debates
Formal speaking practice through role plays and simulation exercises such as meetings, negotiations, technical explanations, job interviews
Writing practice: e-mailing, CVs and cover letters for applications to study/exchange programs or internships including the appropriate use of IA
assessment_rules: The oral exam is in two parts, each making up 25% of the final grade. Continuous evaluation includes two main writing assignments (10% each), and preparation, attendance, and participation (10%). The oral presentation accounts for 20% of the final grade. Attendance is mandatory, and only English may be used. The August/September exam comprises all graded written and oral assignments of the term (presentation 20%, two written assignments 10% each), and the material of the December/January exam (each part 25%). The attendance and participation grade (10%) is retained. The two written assignments are due on the day of the exam at the latest, with no prior feedback.
degree: Bachelor in Engineering (Bachelier en sciences de l'ingénieur, orientation ingénieur civil) - FSA1BA
